title: Example 17-6: Omitted Letters Represented by Hyphens

illustrates.quote: Follow print when hyphens indicate a specific number of missing letters.

print.notes: A single word, letters replaced by a run of seven hyphens between the first and last letter.
surroundingText: (See Sample 17-11: Omitted Letters Identified in Directions on page 17-24.)
print.printFeatures: Omitted letters shown as one hyphen per missing letter.

braille.notes: Neither run's braille.lines was fully correct: A kept a spurious leading space on every line (9-space margin instead of the correct 10) AND wrongly folded the book's own '(See Sample 17-11...)' cross-reference caption (plain print commentary, not braille — it uses ordinary English capitalisation, unlike every real braille-ASCII line around it) into braille.lines; B correctly excluded the caption but is otherwise identical. Re-derived directly from source (line 13640 only, margin 10): single line ';s-------;d', matching B's content exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille: corrected — single line ';s-------;d' (B's version; A had an extra leading space and wrongly appended the print-only 'See Sample 17-11' caption as if it were braille). illustrates.rule: B's '17.9.2b' kept over A's bare '17.9.2' — the example sits directly under clause b's own text (hyphens for a specific letter count).
